HelpRotationText: The Vault never rotates a password automatically. Change the secret on the target system/device first, then update the stored value here.
HelpBreakGlassText: Break Glass identifies an emergency credential and activates the same additional access and audit controls as a Critical credential.

HowToUseCollectionStep1: 1. Set the name and description on the "Basic" tab - pick something that clearly identifies the grouping (team, environment, vendor).
HowToUseCollectionStep2: 2. Grant access to User Groups under Collections > "Access" action - without this, nobody can see this Collection's credentials, not even a module Administrator.
HowToUseCollectionStep3: 3. If you plan to store Tier 0, Tier 1, Critical or Break Glass credentials here, set an Approver Group on the "Basic" tab - without it, those credentials stay blocked in "Pending approver group".
HowToUseCollectionStep4: 4. Add credentials by picking this Collection on the "New Credential" form - they all show up on the "Credentials" tab next to this one.
HowToUseCollectionStep5: 5. To temporarily disable all access to this Collection (without deleting anything), use the "Disable" action on the Collections list.
HowToUseCollectionStep6: 6. Deleting the Collection is permanent and wipes every credential inside it - requires MFA and typing the exact name to confirm.
HelpItemDashboard: The module's home screen: total credentials, Tier 0 count, pending approvals, secrets not updated in 90+ days, technology distribution, quick access to favorites/recent credentials, and the actionable insights panel (weak/reused secrets, credentials without an owner, certificates expiring soon, API keys without an expiration date).
HelpItemAllCredentials: The full, filterable list of every credential you have access to, across all Collections. Filter by category, tier or secret age; open any row for its details, reveal/request-access flow and audit trail.
HelpItemCollectionsIntro: A Collection is both an organizing folder AND the access-control boundary for the credentials inside it - not a cosmetic label. Every credential belongs to exactly one Collection.
HelpItemCollectionsOrg: Organization: group credentials by team, environment, vendor or purpose (e.g. "Windows Licenses", "Network Devices - DC1").
HelpItemCollectionsAccess: Access: granted per User Group, with two levels - View (list/request/reveal per policy) and Manage (also create/edit/disable credentials and configure who has access).
HelpItemCollectionsApprover: Approver Group: optional per Collection, but required for any Tier 0/Tier 1/Critical/Break Glass credential inside it to be usable - without one, those stay "Pending approver group" and can never be revealed.
HelpItemCollectionsNoAccess: No access to a Collection means the credentials inside it are invisible - even to a module Administrator; access is per-Collection, not implied by a broader role.
HelpItemCollectionsDelete: Deleting a Collection permanently deletes every credential inside it - irreversible, and gated behind fresh MFA plus typing the exact Collection name to confirm.
HelpItemRequests: Access requests awaiting approval (or already decided) for protected credentials - Tier 0/Tier 1/Critical/Break Glass always require an approver here; Tier 2/Noncritical credentials skip this and only need MFA.
HelpItemReports: Governance and security report templates for the vault (credential inventory, credentials without an owner, weak/reused secrets, certificates expiring soon), generated on demand from the platform's Reports Center - with scheduling, delivery and history shared with every other report in Hash Access.
HelpItemAudit: The event trail for this module specifically - every reveal, classification change, secret change, access grant/revoke and Collection deletion, each tied to who did it, when, and why (reason/MFA context where applicable).
